readings.title: The Three Hundred Men
readings.subtitle: Gideon's Army is Tested and Triumphs
readings.text:
[Judges 7:1] And Yerubba‛al, that is Giḏ‛on, and all the people who were with <dn>את</dn> him rose up early and encamped by the fountain of Ḥaroḏ, so that the camp of Miḏyan was on the north side of them by the hill of Moreh in the valley.
[2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Giḏ‛on, <dq>The people who are with <dn>את</dn> you are too many for <dn>Me</dn> to give <dn>את</dn> Miḏyan into their hands, lest Yisra’ěl boast against <dn>Me</dn>, saying, ‘My own hand has saved me.’</dq>
[3] <dq>And now, proclaim in the hearing of the people, saying, ‘Whoever is afraid and trembling, let him turn back, and leave Mount Gil‛aḏ.’</dq> And twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, while ten thousand remained.
[4] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Giḏ‛on, <dq>The people are still too many. Bring <dn>את</dn> them down to the water, and let <dn>Me</dn> prove <dn>את</dn> them for you there. And it shall be, that of whom <dn>I</dn> say to you, ‘This one goes with <dn>את</dn> you,’ let him go with <dn>את</dn> you. And of whomever <dn>I</dn> say to you, ‘This one does not go with <dn>את</dn> you,’ let him not go.</dq>
[5] So he brought <dn>את</dn> the people down to the water. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Giḏ‛on, <dq>Everyone who laps the water with his tongue, as a dog laps, separate him from everyone who bows down on his knees to drink.</dq>
[6] And the number of those who lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, was three hundred men, and all the rest of the people bowed down on their knees to drink water.
[7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Giḏ‛on, <dq>By the three hundred men who lapped <dn>I</dn> save <dn>את</dn> you, and shall give <dn>את</dn> Miḏyan into your hand. Let all the other people go, each to his place.</dq>
[8] And the people took <dn>את</dn> food and <dn>את</dn> their shopharot in their hands. And he sent away <dn>את</dn> all the rest of Yisra’ěl, each to his tent, but held onto those three hundred men. Now the camp of Miḏyan was below him in the valley.
[9] And it came to be, on that night, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>Arise, go down against the camp, for <dn>I</dn> have given it into your hand.</dq>
[10] <dq>But if you are afraid to go down, go down, you and Purah your servant, to the camp.</dq>
[11] <dq>And you shall hear what they say, and after that let your hands be strengthened. And you shall go down against the camp.</dq> So he went down with <dn>את</dn> Purah his servant to the edge of the formation of fives who were in the camp.
[12] And Miḏyan and Amalěq, and all the people of the East, were lying in the valley as many as locusts. And their camels were as numerous as the sand by the seashore.
[13] And Giḏ‛on came, and see, a man was relating a dream to his companion, and said, “See I had a dream, and see, a loaf of barley bread tumbled into the camp of Miḏyan, and it came to a tent and struck it so that it fell and overturned, and <dn>את</dn> the tent fell down.”
[14] And his companion answered and said, “This is none other than the sword of Giḏ‛on son of Yo’ash, a man of Yisra’ěl. <dn>Elohim</dn> has given <dn>את</dn> Miḏyan and <dn>את</dn> all the camp into his hand.”
[15] And it came to be, when Giḏ‛on heard <dn>את</dn> this dream related, and <dn>את</dn> its interpretation, that he bowed himself down. And he returned to the camp of Yisra’ěl, and said, “Arise, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given <dn>את</dn> the camp of Miḏyan into your hand.”
[16] And he divided <dn>את</dn> the three hundred men into three companies, and he put shopharot into the hands of all of them, with empty jars, and torches inside the jars.
[17] And he said to them, “Watch me and do likewise. And see, when I come to the edge of the camp do as I do.
[18] “And I shall blow with the shophar, I and all those with <dn>את</dn> me, then you shall also blow with the shopharot round about all the camp, and say, ‘For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and for Giḏ‛on!’ ”
[19] And Giḏ‛on and the hundred men who were with <dn>את</dn> him came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, as they had but newly posted <dn>את</dn> the watch. And they blew with the shopharot and broke the jars that were in their hands.
[20] And the three companies blew with the shopharot and broke the jars, and held the torches in their left hands and the shopharot in their right hands for blowing. And they cried, “A sword for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and for Giḏ‛on!”
[21] And each stood in his place, round about the camp. And all the army ran and cried out and fled,
[22] and the three hundred blew <dn>את</dn> the shopharot, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> set <dn>את</dn> the sword of each one against the other throughout all the camp. And the army fled to Běyth Shittah, toward Tserěrah, as far as the border of Aḇěl Meḥolah, by Tabbath.
[23] And the men of Yisra’ěl were called from Naphtali, and from Ashěr, and from all Menashsheh, and pursued Miḏyan.
[24] Then Giḏ‛on sent messengers throughout all the mountains of Ephrayim, saying, “Come down to meet Miḏyan, and capture from them <dn>את</dn> the watering places as far as Běyth Barah and <dn>את</dn> the Yarděn.” So all the men of Ephrayim were called and captured <dn>את</dn> the watering places as far as Běyth Barah and <dn>את</dn> the Yarděn.
[25] And they captured <dn>את</dn> two princes of Miḏyan, <dn>את</dn> Orěḇ and <dn>את</dn> Ze’ěḇ, and killed <dn>את</dn> Orěḇ at the rock of Orěḇ, and <dn>את</dn> Ze’ěḇ they killed at the winepress of Ze’ěḇ while they pursued Miḏyan. And they brought <dn>את</dn> the heads of Orěḇ and Ze’ěḇ to Giḏ‛on beyond the Yarděn.

readings.subsection: The Pursuit of the Midianite Kings
readings.title: Gideon Defeats Zebah and Zalmunna
readings.subtitle: The Punishment of Succoth and Penuel
readings.text:
[Judges 8:1] And the men of Ephrayim said to him, “What is this you have done to us by not calling us when you went to fight with Miḏyan?” And they contended with <dn>את</dn> him sharply,
[2] and he said to them, “What have I done as compared with you? Are the gleanings of Ephrayim not better than the grape harvest of Aḇi‛ezer?
[3] “<dn>Elohim</dn> has given into your hands <dn>את</dn> the princes of Miḏyan, <dn>את</dn> Orěḇ and <dn>את</dn> Ze’ěḇ. And what was I able to do as compared with you?” And when he had said that their rage toward him subsided.
[4] And Giḏ‛on and the three hundred men who were with <dn>את</dn> him came to the Yarděn, passing over, weary yet pursuing.
[5] And he said to the men of Sukkoth, “Please give loaves of bread to the people who follow me, for they are weary, and I am pursuing <dn>את</dn> Zeḇaḥ and <dn>את</dn> Tsalmunna, sovereigns of Miḏyan.”
[6] But the leaders of Sukkoth said, “Are the hands of Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna now in your hand, that we should give bread to your army?”
[7] And Giḏ‛on said, “Because of this, when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given <dn>את</dn> Zeḇaḥ and <dn>את</dn> Tsalmunna into my hand, I shall tear <dn>את</dn> your flesh with <dn>את</dn> the thorns of the wilderness and with <dn>את</dn> briers!”
[8] And he went up from there to Penu’ěl and spoke to them in the same way. And the men of Penu’ěl answered him as the men of Sukkoth had answered him.
[9] So he spoke also to the men of Penu’ěl, saying, “When I come back in peace I shall break down <dn>את</dn> this tower!”
[10] And Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna were at Qarqor, and their armies with them, about fifteen thousand men, all who were left of all the army of the people of the East. Now those who had already fallen were one hundred and twenty thousand men who drew the sword.
[11] And Giḏ‛on went up by the way of those who dwell in tents on the east of Noḇaḥ and Yoḡbehah. And he struck <dn>את</dn> the camp while the camp was at ease.
[12] And Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna fled, and he pursued them, and captured <dn>את</dn> the two sovereigns of Miḏyan, <dn>את</dn> Zeḇaḥ and <dn>את</dn> Tsalmunna, and shuddered <dn>את</dn> the entire army.
[13] And Giḏ‛on son of Yo’ash returned from battle, from the Ascent of Ḥeres,
[14] and captured a youth of the men of Sukkoth and questioned him. So the youth wrote down for him <dn>את</dn> the leaders of Sukkoth and <dn>את</dn> its elders, seventy-seven men.
[15] And he came to the men of Sukkoth and said, “See: Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, ‘Are the hands of Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna now in your hand, that we should give bread to your men who are weary?’ ”
[16] And he took <dn>את</dn> the elders of the city, and <dn>את</dn> thorns of the wilderness and <dn>את</dn> briers, and with them he taught <dn>את</dn> the men of Sukkoth a lesson.
[17] And he broke down <dn>את</dn> the tower of Penu’ěl and killed <dn>את</dn> the men of the city.
[18] And he said to Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna, “How were the men whom you killed at Taḇor?” So they answered, “They were like you, each one looked like the son of a sovereign .”
[19] And he said, “They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill <dn>את</dn> you.”
[20] And he said to Yether his first-born, “Rise, kill them!” But the youth would not draw his sword, for he was afraid, because he was still a youth.
[21] Then Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna said, “Rise yourself, and fall on us. For as a man is, so is his might.” So Giḏ‛on arose and killed <dn>את</dn> Zeḇaḥ and <dn>את</dn> Tsalmunna, and took <dn>את</dn> the crescent ornaments which were on their camels’ necks.

readings.title: Gideon's Ephod and Death
readings.subtitle: Israel Returns to Idolatry
readings.text:
[Judges 8:22] So the men of Yisra’ěl said to Giḏ‛on, “Rule over us, both you and your son, also your son’s son, for you have saved us from the hand of Miḏyan.”
[23] But Giḏ‛on said to them, “I do not rule over you, nor does my son rule over you. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does rule over you.”
[24] And Giḏ‛on said to them, “I have a request to make of you, that each of you give me the ring from his spoil.” For they had rings of gold, because they were Yishma‛ělites.
[25] And they said, “We shall certainly give them.” And they spread out <dn>את</dn> a garment, and each man threw into it the ring from his spoil.
[26] And the weight of the gold rings that he requested was one thousand seven hundred pieces of gold – besides the crescent ornaments, and the pendants, and purple robes which were on the sovereigns of Miḏyan, and besides the chains that were around their camels’ necks.
[27] And Giḏ‛on made <dn>את</dn> it into a shoulder garment and set it up in his city, Ophrah. And all Yisra’ěl went whoring after it there. And it became a snare to Giḏ‛on and to his house.
[28] Thus Miḏyan was humbled before the children of Yisra’ěl, and they lifted their heads no more. And the land had rest for forty years in the days of Giḏ‛on.
[29] And Yerubba‛al son of Yo’ash went and dwelt in his own house.
[30] And Giḏ‛on had seventy sons who were his own offspring, for he had many wives.
[31] And his concubine who was in Sheḵem also bore him a son, and he gave him <dn>את</dn> the name Aḇimeleḵ.
[32] And Giḏ‛on son of Yo’ash died at a good old age, and was buried in the burial-site of Yo’ash his father, in Ophrah of the Aḇi‛ezerites.
[33] And it came to be, when Giḏ‛on was dead, that the children of Yisra’ěl again went whoring after the Ba‛als, and made Ba‛al-Berith their mighty one.
[34] Thus the children of Yisra’ěl did not remember <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, who had delivered <dn>את</dn> them from the hands of all their enemies round about,
[35] nor did they show loving-commitment to the house of Yerubba‛al, Giḏ‛on, according to all the good which he did for Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: Abimelech's Conspiracy and Jotham's Parable
readings.subtitle: The Bramble King
readings.text:
[Judges 9:1] And Aḇimeleḵ son of Yerubba‛al went to Sheḵem, to his mother’s brothers, and spoke with them and with all the clan of the house of his mother’s father, saying,
[2] “Please speak in the hearing of all the masters of Sheḵem, ‘Which is better for you, that seventy men, all the sons of Yerubba‛al rule over you, or that one man rule over you?’ And you shall remember that I am your own flesh and bone.”
[3] And his mother’s brothers spoke <dn>את</dn> all these words concerning him in the hearing of all the masters of Sheḵem. And their heart inclined toward Aḇimeleḵ, for they said, “He is our brother.”
[4] And they gave him seventy pieces of silver from the house of Ba‛al-Berith, with which Aḇimeleḵ hired worthless and reckless men. And they followed him.
[5] And he went to his father’s house at Ophrah and killed <dn>את</dn> his brothers, the seventy sons of Yerubba‛al, on one stone. But Yotham the youngest son of Yerubba‛al was left, because he hid himself.
[6] And all the masters of Sheḵem gathered together, and all of Běyth Millo, and they went and made <dn>את</dn> Aḇimeleḵ sovereign beside the terebinth tree at the post that was in Sheḵem.
[7] And they informed Yotham, and he went and stood on top of Mount Gerizim, and lifted his voice and cried out, and said to them, “Hear me, you masters of Sheḵem, and let <dn>Elohim</dn> hear you!
[8] “The trees went forth to anoint a sovereign over them. And they said to the olive tree, ‘reign over us!’
[9] “And the olive tree said to them, ‘Shall I leave <dn>את</dn> my oil, with which they esteem mighty ones and men, and go to sway over trees?’
[10] “Then the trees said to the fig tree, ‘Come, reign over us!’
[11] “And the fig tree said to them, ‘Shall I leave <dn>את</dn> my sweetness and <dn>את</dn> my good fruit, and go to sway over trees?’
[12] “Then the trees said to the vine, ‘Come, reign over us!’
[13] “And the vine said to them, ‘Shall I leave <dn>את</dn> my new wine, which rejoices mighty ones and men, and go to sway over trees?’
[14] “Then all the trees said to the bramble, ‘Come, reign over us!’
[15] “And the bramble said to the trees, ‘If in truth you anoint <dn>את</dn> me as sovereign over you, come, take shelter in my shade. But if not, let fire come out of the bramble and devour <dn>את</dn> the cedars of Leḇanon!’
[16] “And now, if you have acted in truth and integrity in setting up <dn>את</dn> Aḇimeleḵ to reign, and if you have acted well with Yerubba‛al and his house, and have done to him as his hands did to you –
[17] for my father fought for you and risked <dn>את</dn> his life, and delivered <dn>את</dn> you out of the hand of Miḏyan,
[18] but you have risen up against my father’s house today, and killed <dn>את</dn> his seventy sons on one stone, and set up <dn>את</dn> Aḇimeleḵ, the son of his female servant, to reign over the masters of Sheḵem, because he is your brother –
[19] if then you have acted in truth and integrity with Yerubba‛al and with his house this day, then rejoice in Aḇimeleḵ, and let him also rejoice in you.
[20] “But if not, let fire come out from Aḇimeleḵ and devour <dn>את</dn> the masters of Sheḵem and <dn>את</dn> Běyth Millo, and let fire come out from the masters of Sheḵem and from Běyth Millo and devour <dn>את</dn> Aḇimeleḵ!”
[21] Then Yotham ran away and fled, and he went to Be’ěr and dwelt there, for fear of Aḇimeleḵ his brother.

readings.title: The Destruction of Shechem
readings.subtitle: The Death of the Bramble King
readings.text:
[Judges 9:22] And Aḇimeleḵ governed Yisra’ěl three years,
[23] and <dn>Elohim</dn> sent an evil spirit between Aḇimeleḵ and the masters of Sheḵem. And the masters of Sheḵem acted treacherously against Aḇimeleḵ,
[24] in order that the violence done to the seventy sons of Yerubba‛al might come, and their blood be laid on Aḇimeleḵ their brother, who killed <dn>את</dn> them, and on the masters of Sheḵem, who strengthened <dn>את</dn> his hands to kill <dn>את</dn> his brothers.
[25] And the masters of Sheḵem set men in ambush against him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed <dn>את</dn> all who passed over by them along that way. And it was reported to Aḇimeleḵ.
[26] And Ga‛al son of Eḇeḏ came with his brothers and passed over to Sheḵem. And the masters of Sheḵem put their trust in him,
[27] and went out into the fields, and gathered <dn>את</dn> their vineyards and trod out, and held a feast. And they went into the house of their mighty one, and ate and drank, and cursed <dn>את</dn> Aḇimeleḵ.
[28] And Ga‛al son of Eḇeḏ said, “Who is Aḇimeleḵ, and who is Sheḵem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Yerubba‛al, and is not Zeḇul his officer? Serve <dn>את</dn> the men of Ḥamor the father of Sheḵem! But why should we serve him?
[29] “If only <dn>את</dn> this people were under my hand! Then I would remove <dn>את</dn> Aḇimeleḵ.” And he said to Aḇimeleḵ, “Increase <dn>את</dn> your army and come out!”
[30] And when Zeḇul, the governor of the city, heard <dn>את</dn> the words of Ga‛al son of Eḇeḏ, his displeasure burned.
[31] And he sent messengers to Aḇimeleḵ by deceit, saying, “See, Ga‛al son of Eḇeḏ and his brothers have come to Sheḵem. And see, they are besieging <dn>את</dn> the city against you.
[32] “And now, get up by night, you and the people who are with <dn>את</dn> you, and lie in wait in the field.
[33] “And it shall be, as soon as the sun is up in the morning, then rise early and rush upon the city. And see, when he and the people who are with <dn>את</dn> him come out against you, you shall do to them as your hand finds to do.”
[34] And Aḇimeleḵ and all the people who were with <dn>את</dn> him rose up by night, and laid in wait against Sheḵem in four companies.
[35] Now Ga‛al son of Eḇeḏ went out and stood in the entrance to the city gate, and Aḇimeleḵ and the people who were with <dn>את</dn> him rose from lying in wait.
[36] And when Ga‛al saw <dn>את</dn> the people, he said to Zeḇul, “See, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains!” But Zeḇul said to him, “You are seeing <dn>את</dn> the shadows of the mountains like men.”
[37] And Ga‛al spoke again and said, “See, people are coming down from the high part of the land, and another company is coming from the Diviners’ Terebinth Tree.”
[38] And Zeḇul said to him, “Now where is your mouth with which you said, ‘Who is Aḇimeleḵ, that we should serve him?’ Are not these the people whom you despised? I beg you, go out and fight them now.”
[39] So Ga‛al went out, leading the masters of Sheḵem, and fought Aḇimeleḵ.
[40] And Aḇimeleḵ pursued him, and he fled from him. And many fell wounded, up to the entrance of the gate.
[41] And Aḇimeleḵ stayed at Arumah, and Zeḇul drove out <dn>את</dn> Ga‛al and <dn>את</dn> his brothers, so that they would not dwell in Sheḵem.
[42] And it came to be the next day that the people went out into the field, and they informed Aḇimeleḵ.
[43] And he took <dn>את</dn> his people, and divided them into three companies, and laid in wait in the field, and looked and saw the people coming out of the city. And he rose against them and struck them.
[44] And Aḇimeleḵ and the company that was with <dn>את</dn> him rushed forward and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city. And the other two companies rushed upon all who were in the fields and struck them.
[45] And Aḇimeleḵ fought against the city all that day, and captured <dn>את</dn> the city and killed <dn>את</dn> the people who were in it. And he broke down <dn>את</dn> the city and sowed it with salt.
[46] And all the masters of the tower of Sheḵem had heard that, and entered the stronghold of the house of Ěl Berith.
[47] And it was reported to Aḇimeleḵ that all the masters of the tower of Sheḵem were gathered together.
[48] So Aḇimeleḵ went up to Mount Tsalmon, he and all the people who were with <dn>את</dn> him. And Aḇimeleḵ took <dn>את</dn> an axe in his hand and cut down <dn>את</dn> a branch from the trees, and took it and laid it on his shoulder. Then he said to the people who were with <dn>את</dn> him, “What you have seen me do, hurry, do as I have done.”
[49] And all the people likewise cut down each one his own branch and followed Aḇimeleḵ, and put them against the stronghold, and set the stronghold on fire above them, so that all the men of the tower of Sheḵem died, about a thousand men and women.
[50] Aḇimeleḵ then went to Thěḇěts, and he encamped against Thěḇěts and captured it.
[51] However, there was a strong tower in the city, and all the men and women and all the masters of the city fled there and shut themselves in, and went up to the top of the tower.
[52] And Aḇimeleḵ came to the tower and fought against it, and approached the door of the tower to burn it with fire.
[53] But a certain woman dropped an upper millstone on the head of Aḇimeleḵ, and crushed <dn>את</dn> his skull.
[54] He then immediately called the young man, his armour-bearer, and said to him, “Draw your sword and kill me, lest men say of me, ‘A woman killed him.’ ” And his young man thrust him through, and he died.
[55] And when the men of Yisra’ěl saw that Aḇimeleḵ was dead, each one went to his own place.
[56] Thus did <dn>Elohim</dn> repay <dn>את</dn> the evil of Aḇimeleḵ, which he had done to his father to kill his seventy brothers.
[57] And <dn>את</dn> all the evil of the men of Sheḵem <dn>Elohim</dn> turned back on their own heads, and the curse of Yotham son of Yerubba‛al came on them.
